pageCache.pageTitle: St John's, Gosport Church of England Voluntary Aided Primary School - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Vision and Values
Our Christian Values As a Church of England Voluntary Aided School, we have very close connections with St. John's Forton. We often visit the church for whole school services and for R.E. lessons. Father Godfrey and his team also visit the school for Collective Worship and to talk to the children.
Our Christian Values LOVE, COURAGE and RESPECT are at the centre of everything we do at St John's C of E Primary School. They help us to live out our Christian Vision of ‘life in all its fullness’. Each half term, we focus on a different Christian Value. This is done explicitly through our Collective Worship time, but also throughout our curriculum. Children have regular opportunities to reflect on each value and to develop an understanding of the Value in action. Each Friday, in our Celebration Collective Worship, we acknowledge children who have demonstrated these values.
Our Vision for St John’s promotes: Preparing the next generation to flourish and prosper in all aspects of life:
Promoting Fundamental British Values In accordance with The Department for Education we aim to actively promote British values in schools to ensure young people leave school prepared for life in modern Britain. Pupils are encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right’ and ‘wrong’, all people living in England are subject to its law.

SEND at St John's
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Provision
St John’s Primary School is a Church of England mainstream school. We are highly committed to offering an inclusive curriculum to ensure the best possible progress for all of our pupils, whatever their needs and abilities.
The school seeks to raise the achievement, remove barriers to learning and support physical and curricular access to all.
We aim to enable every child to learn as effectively as possible, to enjoy his/her learning and to provide a foundation for life-long learning.
All children with Special Educational Needs or Disabilities (SEND) are valued, respected and are equal members of the school.
Our SENDCo is Mrs Chambers who also runs the The Inclusion Team.
Mrs Rose is our Behaviour Support Lead; she works with parents on referrals to CAMHS and Primary Behaviour Support Service.
Mrs Blanksby is the Family Support Worker (FSW) and school ELSA.
Ms Hyndman is our attendance office and also another ELSA in school.
We have a SEN LSA Mrs Roberts who specialises in 'Speech and Language.'
Further information about SEND provision at St John's Primary School can be found in our SEND policy and SEN Information Report on this website.

Mental Health
Inclusion day 2023
We held an Inclusion day in school at the end of September. Mrs James organised a fab and fun filled day for the whole school to take part in, along with Portsmouth in the Community (Mr Plow_ and the sports leaders from School.
The playground was an array of colours as the children arrived in different colours of the rainbow.
They started the day with an assembly all about inclusion, and practiced the song ‘Rise Up; using Makaton signing, which Key Stage 2 children then performed to parents at the end of the day. We had a visit from the Portsmouth mascot Nelson, along with ex footballer, Alan Knight.
On top of this, the Makaton Choir then gave a lovely performance of their songs to the parents this afternoon.
Well done children, we are very proud of you. – Inclusion day was a fine example of St Johns doing what St John’s does best!

pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Dear Parents and Carers
On behalf of the governors and staff of St John’s Gosport Church of England (Voluntary Aided) , I would like to welcome you to our school website.
At St John’s we pride ourselves on providing high quality care and education guided by our Christian values: Love, Courage and Respect. We offer a blend of the traditional and the contemporary; a safe, secure and well-resourced environment which fosters respect for self, other children, adults and the environment. Children are able to experience enjoyment of school and celebrate the attainment of their full and highest capability in a creative and joyous learning atmosphere.
We are an inclusive school and we also work hard to preserve the school’s cultural roots, teaching children to know their own heritage, but at the same time learning to understand and respect the different backgrounds of others. As a Church of England school we seek to achieve our aims within the context of the Christian faith, keeping true to the school’s Christian foundation and purpose. However, we warmly welcome children of families from all backgrounds, whose parents/carers will support the education of their children in a school with clear values, a family-centred approach and high standards.
Our professional team is highly motivated to provide children with a broad-based and challenging learning experience. We are committed to nurturing children’s spiritual, academic, moral and social development. For us, the education process is a ’golden triangle.’ This means the child, the parents and the school, all work together to ensure every child receives the maximum benefit from their education. Parents who choose St. John’s find that if they or their children have any concerns, we will always listen. We value parents’ opinions on the school and on their child’s achievements. Of course, we always listen to children’s views and value their thoughts and feedback too.
We hope that this website will give you as much information as possible about our school and a flavour of what we can offer your children and family. If you have any further questions or need more information, please contact us through the school office.
Headteacher's Welcome

Admissions
If you are interested in applying for a school place in any year group at St Johns Primary School and would like to take a look around, please call the school office on 02392 582 404 to arrange a tour.
Applying for a Year R Place Starting in September?
If you are applying for a Year R place as part of the main round admissions, these applications are processed by the County Admissions Team. You can apply online via the Hampshire Admissions Portal - Click Here - If you would prefer, you can complete a paper copy of the Year R application form at school, and we can forward it to the County Admissions Team on your behalf.
The application time frame opens in November and closes in January.
We have a dedicated page for New Year R children - click here for more information YEAR R
Alternatively you can contact the Admissions Team at: County Admissions Team Children's Services Department The Castle Winchester Hampshire SO23 8UG
Tel: 0300 555 1377 email: admissions.team@hants.gov.uk
Applying for a school place during the school year?
If you would like to apply for a place outside of the main round admissions, this can be done via the County Admissions Team, or directly to the school. Please call the school office on 02392 582 404, who will be happy to assist you. The application form can be found on the Hampshire admissions website , this process is called an 'in year transfer'. We do have paper application forms available in our school office.
As of January 2026 we have the following space
Year R - 0 spaces / Year 1 - 2 Spaces / Year 2 - 7 Spaces / Year 3 - 1 Space / Year 4 - 5 Spaces / Year 5 - 0 Spaces / Year 6 - 2 Spaces
If a year group is full or over subscribed, applicants are placed on our waiting list. Places are allocated using the criteria set out by Hampshire County Council. Please see the Admissions Policy for more details.
For further information regarding the selection criteria used to allocate school places, please contact the County Admissions Team on 0300 555 1377.
Admissions policy
You can check Hampshire County Council's website for more information. Our admission policies are below.
Please note, the Hampshire County Council website only shows our Local Authority Catchment area. St Johns also have an additional Catchment which is linked to our Parish. This Catchment map can also be found below and on Hampshire's website.
